text: Graviton is a minor antagonist in The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes. Graviton was created by Jim Shooter and Sal Buscema.
Grotta is a bossy fliegel, who appears in the Sofia the First episode "The Fliegel Has Landed" as the main antagonist.
Granite is a character from the Disney Channel animated series Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur. He is a superhero who fought crime with his pet dog, Pebble whom he adores a lot.
Darkmoon was an ancient and evil temple, located on the Sword Coast.
Hangry Panda is a recurring antagonist in the third and final season of Big Hero 6: The Series. She is a robotic panda with an attitude and anger problem.
He-Lectrix (real name Tom Current) is a character in Disney/Pixar's 2018 animated film Incredibles 2, who is part of a group of new Supers who aspire to join the ranks of superheroes.
Hardlight is a villain in Big Hero 6: The Series. His real name is Ian, who works as a scientist at Krei Tech Industries. His specialty is force field engineering.
Dancing blade was a common spell used by wu jen in Kara-Tur. The spell was very rare outside Kara-Tur.

He Who Remains is a Marvel Comics character and the main antagonist of the Loki series. He is a Variant of Kang the Conqueror and is the one behind the Time Variance Authority. He Who Remains was created by Len Wein, Joe Sinnott, and John Buscema.

Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz is the main antagonist of the Disney Channel animated series Phineas and Ferb. He is a mad scientist, who once plotted to rule over the Tri-State Area with the power of his eccentric inventions (referred to as "-Inators"). Doofenshmirtz‘s schemes were consistently foiled by the efforts of his "nemesis" Perry the Platypus, a fedora-wearing secret agent. After numerous failed attempts at domination, Doofenshmirtz eventually retired from villainy and reformed, but would return to villainy in the series' revival almost a decade later before retiring from it again this time once and for all afterwards. In the interim he also became a recurring character in Milo Murphy's Law as a resident of the Murphy household and a friend to Vinnie Dakota.
Barb and Juniper are a mother-daughter criminal duo known as High Voltage in Big Hero 6: The Series.
Darkmail was a suit of enchanted chainmail armor that was found in the Realms during the 14 century DR.

The Horned King is the main antagonist of Disney's 1985 animated feature film The Black Cauldron. He is a powerful demonic being who sought to find the Black Cauldron and use its power to unleash an army of deathless warriors called the Cauldron Born. The Horned King has a vast army under him, which includes the troll-like Creeper, the hunters of Annuvin, the draconic Gwythaints, and, obviously, the Cauldron Born.
Hydro-Man is a water-based supervillain that appeares in Ultimate Spider-Man vs. The Sinister 6. Hydro-Man was created by Dennis O'Neil and John Romita Jr.
Iron Fist (real name Daniel "Danny" Thomas Rand) is a martial artist superhero from Marvel Comics. Iron Fist was created by Roy Thomas and Gil Kane.
Damays was a tiefling from Elturel who lived on the Sword Coast for a time during the 15 century DR.

Princess Ingrid, also known as the Snow Queen is the main antagonist in the first half of the fourth season of ABC's series Once Upon a Time, and the maternal aunt of Elsa and Anna. She debuts in the second episode of the fourth season. Ingrid is based on the titular character of the same name from the fairy tale "".

John Jackson "Jack-Jack" Parr is a major character in the 2004 Disney•Pixar animated film The Incredibles and its 2018 sequel, as well as a main character in the short films Jack-Jack Attack and Auntie Edna. He is the youngest child of Bob and Helen and the younger brother of Violet and Dash. Despite coming from a family of Supers, it was initially believed that he was born without any powers. In a surprising turn of events, the Parrs would later discover that he has at least seventeen powers.
Ixlan is a Maruvian warrior who appears in the Disney Channel animated series Elena of Avalor. She is the only living Maruvian and is also known as the Lightning Warrior.

Darndarr was a type of ale renowned for its nutty taste and ease of storage and transportation. Darndarr was popular all throughout the Sword Coast the late 15 century DR for both casual consumption and use in marinades.

Jane Foster (also known as Mighty Thor) is the deuteragonist of Thor, Thor: The Dark World, and Thor: Love and Thunder. She is a brilliant astronomer and cosmologist, and also Thor's partner and love interest. She is portrayed by Natalie Portman. After eight years apart, Jane and Thor rekindled their relationship, but she passed away due to her cancer disease and passed on to Valhalla, after dying in a battle against Gorr the God Butcher. Jane Foster was created by Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, and Larry Lieber.
Jade (pronounced 'Ha-day') is a gargoyle member of the Mayan Clan. He appears in the Disney animated TV series Gargoyles. His name is derived from the Mayan pendant he wears.
Lady Lightbug is the main antagonist of the DVD short film Mr. Incredible and Pals.
The Dance Blade of the Seven Winds was an enchanted ceremonial dagger that belonged to the aarakocras of Kir Sabal in the late 15 century DR.

Lea is one of the major characters of the Kingdom Hearts series. Lea has a desire to achieve his own ideal of immortality by having everyone remember his name. He was once Axel, a member of Organization XIII who served as its assassin, until the destruction of both Axel and his Heartless that allowed Lea to be reborn. Since then, Lea has become an ally of Sora and was revealed to be able to wield a Keyblade.

The Lizard is the alter ego of Dr. Curtis "Curt" Connors, originating from Marvel Comics. He appears as an antagonist in the film Spider-Man: No Way Home, played by Rhys Ifans, reprising his role from The Amazing Spider-Man. The Lizard was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.
Magenta, also known as "Maj", is a supporting character in the film Sky High.
Dancer's Silhouette was a type of powerful enchanted light armor created specifically for shadowdancers' use.
Magma is a fire elemental ifrit who appears in the Aladdin TV series episode "Smolder and Wiser".

Luna Girl (also called Luna for short) is the secondary antagonist (sometimes an anti-heroine) from the Disney Jr. show PJ Masks. She is one of the nighttime villains. She is always followed by moths, known as Luna Moths, throughout the show.
Lyn Rakish (also known as the Fourth Sister) is an Nogratu Jedi who became an Imperial Inquisitor, who appears in the Star Wars franchise.
Darney was a dwarven geologist that lived on the Sword Coast North region of Faerûn during the late 15 century DR.

The Evil Manta, or just Manta, is a major antagonist who appears in Disney's animated TV series The Little Mermaid. Although it is unknown how old he is, he is believed to be ageless. He has the form of a giant black and purple manta ray, giving a foul presence wherever he dwells.
Mariko Takeda is the older daughter of Takeda, who discovered a parallel dimension and was sentenced into a magical slumber. She later reawakened as a powerful vigilante called the Black Queen.
Matangi is a supporting character in Disney's 2024 animated feature film Moana 2. She is a crafty and mysterious demigoddess who serves as an enforcer for Nalo, the storm god.
The Dancing Delight was a corsair owned by the Tabaxi captain Stands in Tar. The ship plied the Sea of Swords in the late 15 century DR, hauling goods for merchants as well as passengers.

Megavolt (real name Elmo Sputterspark) is a recurring antagonist of the Darkwing Duck franchise. He is an insane anthropomorphic rat with the ability to control electricity and a former classmate of Darkwing Duck's in high school, where he gained his powers after bullies sabotaged his science experiment. He is additionally a member of Negaduck's Fearsome Five.

Mega-Hulk (real name Bruce Banner) is a character who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe animated series What If...? He is an alternate variant of Hulk who appears in "What If... The Hulk Fought the Mech Avengers?", where he tried to get rid of the Hulk by bombarding himself with gamma radiation, but ended up accidentally creating Gamma Beasts. Hulk was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

Melvin is the main antagonist of Disney's 2005 animated feature film Chicken Little. He is an alien who is Kirby's father and Tina's husband, who caused an alien invasion on Oakey Oaks after his son was missing from him and his wife.
The darksteel greataxe was an axe that came to be wielded by the barbarian Holga Kilgore in the late 1490s DR.
Merlin was a great and powerful wizard, and the overarching protagonist from the film The Sorcerer's Apprentice.

Mephisto is a Marvel Comics supervillain who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He first appears in the series Ironheart and is portrayed by Sacha Baron Cohen. This version of Mephisto was created by Stan Lee and Jerry Robinson.

The Minotaur is a mythical creature who appears in the 1997 Disney animated feature film Hercules and its television series. He is a large humanoid bull who resided in an endless maze within the city of Knossos, the capital of Crete.
Danley and Sons Inn was the only inn tavern located in the resettled town of Phandalin on the Sword Coast North in the late 14 century DR.

Miss Piggy is one of the central characters of the Muppets franchise. She developed from a one-joke running gag into a Muppet herself. Miss Piggy is a prima-donna pig who is absolutely convinced that she's destined for stardom, and nothing is going to stand in her way. Her public face is the soul of feminine charm, but she can instantly fly into a violent rage whenever she thinks she's insulted or thwarted. Kermit the Frog, her longtime crush has learned this all too well; when she isn't smothering him in kisses, she's sending him flying through the air with a karate-chop.

Monstro is a gigantic and ferocious sperm whale and the fourth and final antagonist to appear in Disney's 1940 animated feature film Pinocchio. Dwelling in the depths of the ocean, Monstro is a creature of monstrous proportions and is infamous for swallowing anything in his path. He is approximately 252½ feet (77 meters) long, 65½ feet (20 meters) at his thickest point, and 4,500 short tons (4,082.4 metric tons) in mass. His teeth are about 2½ feet (76.2 centimeters) long.

Molten Man is a Marvel Comics character who appears in the Disney XD animated series Ultimate Spider-Man. He is a prominent supervillain of Spider-Man. Molten Man was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.
Darhabran Windhome was a caravan guard in the Sword Coast during the mid-14 century DR.

Molecule Man is a Marvel Comics character that appeared in Avengers Assemble and as the secondary antagonist in Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur. He is a supervillain with the ability to alter the molecules of one thing to another. Molecule Man was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.
Mr. Dark (also known as The Illustrated Man and The Illustrated Marvel), is a character and the main antagonist of Disney's 1983 live-action film Something Wicked This Way Comes.

Motsuki and formerly nicknamed Henchman Moth, is an insectoid and Luna Girl's sister. She is an antagonist (but also, like her big sister, an anti-hero) in the television series PJ Masks. Motsuki first appeared in "Moon Madness", as one of Luna Girl's many moths. After helping Luna Girl steal the Moon Crystal from PJ Masks Headquarters, Luna Girl decided to promote her to her new henchman, and used the crystal to give her a name, a new appearance, and some powers. Then in "Moth on the Moon", Motsuki decided to go to the Moon to become Luna Girl's new sister by forming a strange Moon Crystal in a cave to hibernate, fueled by negative energy, to hatch her into a humanoid-like moth.
Dame Guisarme was a fighter-adventurer and a mercenary patron of the Elfsong Tavern from the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Mulch, also known as Experiment 111, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to tear up the ground beneath his feet. His one true place is with Mrs. Hasagawa as one of her "cats".

Multi-Bear is a large magical beast whom Dipper went to conquer in order to attain manliness. It has eight heads, with one main, intelligent head, capable of human speech. It lives in the Multi-Bear's cave at the top of a high mountain.
Myron Brogan, better known as The Incredible Bulk, is a character from the Goof Troop episode of the same name.
Danzo Arkwright was the dwarf in charge of the Sword Coast Couriers in the Rivington neighborhood of the Outer City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Namor, also known as K'uk'ulkan, and born as Ch'ah Toh Almehen, is a Marvel Comics character who debuted in the Marvel Cinematic Universe in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, serving as the main antagonist. He is the king of Talokan and a mutant. Namor is drawn to the surface by the ramifications of T'Challa's decision to reveal the truth of Wakanda to the world, which puts Talokan in jeopardy. Namor was created by Bill Everett.

Virginia "Pepper" Stark (nee Potts) is the deuteragonist of the Iron Man film series, a supporting character in The Avengers film series and a cameo character in Spider-Man: Homecoming. She is Tony Stark's personal secretary, executive assistant, eventually girlfriend and later wife. She gained superpowers after being bonded to the Extremis formula by Aldrich Killian in Iron Man 3, but is cured by Tony. She later appears as the superheroine Rescue in Avengers: Endgame, utilizing a nanotech armor built for her by Tony. Pepper Potts was created by Stan Lee and Don Heck.

Pepa Madrigal is a supporting character in Disney's 2021 animated feature film Encanto. She is the middle child of Alma and Pedro Madrigal and the mother of Dolores, Camilo, and Antonio, whom she parented alongside her husband, Félix. Described as "overly emotional and dramatic", Pepa's gift allows her to control the weather via her emotions.

Dargathan Srune'Lett was a young male drow fighter who learned at the academy of Melee Magthere. He tutored the novice priestess Liriel Baenre and taught her fighting with a sword during her time at Arach-Tinilith.
Perseus "Percy" Jackson is the titular protagonist in the Disney+ series Percy Jackson and the Olympians. He is the half-blood son of Poseidon who discovers his destiny.

Porco Rosso is the protagonist from the 1992 film on the same name. He is an ex-World War I fighter pilot, now living as a freelance bounty hunter chasing "air pirates" in the Adriatic Sea. However, an unusual curse has transformed him to an anthropomorphic pig. Once called Marco Pagot, he is now known to the world as "Porco Rosso", Italian for "Red Pig". He was originally voiced by Shūichirō Moriyama in Japanese and was voiced by Michael Keaton in the English dub.

Polaris (real name Lorna Dane) is a Marvel Comics character who appeared in and X-Men '97. She is a Mutant who can control magnetism like her father, Magneto. She is also a former member of the X-Men who went on to join the mutant team known as the X-Factor. During the period when anti-mutant sentiment was rising and X-Factor had come under U.S. government control, Polaris was ultimately dismissed due to her dangerous behavior, leading her to return to the X-Men. Polaris was created by Arnold Drake and Werner Roth.
Death ward was a magical quality that could be applied to armor to protect its wearer from death magic.
Proteus is a villain of the Disney animated TV series Gargoyles. He is a sadistic, shapeshifting New Olympian criminal and murderer.
Prisma is the main antagonist of the fourth season of the Disney Jr. animated series Sofia the First. She is a devious and jealous Crystalmaster who is a enemy of the EverRealm's protectors.

The Queen of Atlantis is a character in Atlantis: The Lost Empire. She is the wife of King Kashekim Nedakh and the mother of Princess Kida Nedakh. She is also the mother-in-law of Milo Thatch. When her daughter was a young girl, the Queen was chosen, unwillingly, by the Heart of Atlantis to protect the city. Having stayed bonded too long, she was lost to the crystal. When Kida was released from the crystal, the former Queen was present enough to return Kida's bracelet to her. This act also gave her only child a lot of closure for her passing.
Dawnspeaker was the favored weapon of Lathander, Faerûnian god of the morning. It was a +5 disruption ghost touch holy heavy mace.

Agent Daisy Johnson is a Marvel Comics character best known as the superheroine Quake. She appears in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., initially known as Skye. Quake was created by Brian Michael Bendis and Gabriele Dell'Otto.

Quetzalcoatl is a deity who serves as one of the major deities of Mesoamerican culture. He serves as one of the most important figures within Mesoamerican culture serving as the god of winds and rain as well as the creator of the world and humanity. Despite being one of the most important deities in Mesoamerican culture, he makes uncommon to rare appearances in Disney properties.

Ra is the Egyptian God of the Sun and the King of the Egyptian Gods, who appears in the Hercules episode "Hercules and the Romans". Alongside Bastet and Khnum, Ra meets the request by the Romans for worshiping deities. But when the three Egyptians arrive to the Eternal City, it is revealed that their real intent is to mold it in the image of their homeland - and, for that, enslave the citizens.
A dart is a small sharp implement intended to be used as a ranged weapon, either to be thrown or blown from a blowpipe.
Reina Carvajal is a character that appears in Upside-Down Magic. She is a Flare and Nory's best friend.

Reuben, also known as Experiment 625, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba, a frequent henchman of Gantu, and a major character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise, first appearing in Stitch! The Movie. He is the last failed prototype of Stitch. He possesses all of Stitch's powers and is equipped with advanced linguistic skills. The main flaws in his programming are cowardice and laziness; the most strenuous thing he ever does is make sandwiches, albeit delicious ones. His one true place is with Gantu as his galley officer and chef.

Retro, also known as Experiment 210, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to reduce individuals, animals, enemy weapons, and technology to their primitive or prehistoric state; wrapping his tongue around the de-evolved object or victim and spanking his bottom three times will reverse the transformation. His one true place is at a wildlife park, resurrecting extinct animals for a Mesozoic zoo.
The Dead Rats were a street gang operating in Luskan and Neverwinter on the northern Sword Coast. The Dead Rats were loosely allied with the Coin Spinners gang.

Rocket Raccoon (real name 89P13) is a Marvel Comics superhero that appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He is one of the titular protagonists of the Guardians of the Galaxy film series. Rocket is an anthropomorphic raccoon with expert marksmanship and is a member of the Guardians of the Galaxy, and also has anger issues. In Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, he becomes the new leader of a new team of Guardians. Rocket Raccoon was created by Bill Mantlo and Keith Giffen.

Rumplewatt the Giant was the main antagonist to Mickey Mouse in the animated short Giantland, where he plays the part of the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk in a version of the story Mickey is telling to a group of orphans. Though a one-shot character in animated shorts, he did make a few appearances in comic books and has a cameo role in a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_%26_Watch Game & Watch] inspired minigame in Kingdom Hearts III.
The Sand Monster is a minor villain in the Disney animated series Aladdin. He was a massive sand creature created by Sadira with a mystical amulet.
Decastave was an evocation/conjuration spell that converted a small piece of wood into a force-staff that could be wielded as a magic weapon.

Sana Ali is a character from Marvel Comics, who appears within the Marvel Cinematic Universe. She was first mentioned in the first episode, before making her debut in the second episode of the Disney+ series Ms. Marvel. She is primarily portrayed by starring cast member, Samina Ahmad, while Zion Usman plays her during the flashback sequences. Sana is the daughter of man named Hasan, and Aisha who was a Djinn. Through her mixed lineage, she held some form of powers. During the Partition of India, she was separated from her parents, but a trail of stars reunited her with her father. She went on to become mother to Muneeba, and grandmother to Aamir and Kamala Khan. When she sends her family in New Jersey, a box of her old belongings, Kamala puts on her bangle, which unlocks her powers. Sana later receives a vision of the train she boarded during the Partition, and calls her granddaughter to visit her in Pakistan, after she received the same vision too. Sana Ali was originally created by writer G. Willow Wilson and artists Takeshi Miyazawa and Adrian Alphona.

Scott Lang (also known as Ant-Man) is a superhero from Marvel Comics and the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He is the titular main protagonist of Ant-Man, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania, while also appearing in Captain America: Civil War, Avengers: Endgame, and Avengers: Doomsday. A former criminal and reluctant hero, Scott succeeded Hank Pym as the second Ant-Man, as well as Giant-Man. Scott Lang was created by David Michelinie and John Byrne.
Simon is a sea dragon and a one-time character in the episode "Message in a Bottle" of Disney's animated series The Little Mermaid.
A death spear or death lance was a longspear infused with negative energy and used by elite drow warriors.

Sinara is a character on the ABC series, Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.. She is a female Kree in the year 2091 that serves as Kasius' second-in-command, enforcer, and head of the Kree Watch. She wields floating spheres which she uses to either attack her enemies or kill anyone that has offended Kasius. She makes her first appearance in "Orientation (Part Two)", and is portrayed by Florence Faivre.

Sibyl is a character featured on the Marvel/ABC series Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. She is the Head Chronicom, and their Predictor, with the ability to foretell possible outcomes, based on probability. She works with the Chronicom Hunters, to prevent the formation of S.H.I.E.L.D., and establish a new homeland on Earth. She is portrayed by Tamara, and makes her first appearance in the season seven episode "Alien Commies from the Future!" Sibyl was created by Jed Whedon and Maurissa Tancharoen.

Shego is the secondary antagonist, and occasional anti-hero, from Disney's Kim Possible. She frequently fights Kim Possible, being her primary combatant and most dangerous opponent. Under contract as an evil sidekick, Dr. Drakken is her usual employer, although she has occasionally (temporarily) worked with other villains.
Dauravyn Redbeard was an innkeeper who lived on the Sword Coast in the mid–14 century DR.

Skylar Storm is a main character in Disney XD's Mighty Med and Lab Rats: Elite Force. To the general public she is a comic book character that Kaz and Oliver like. In reality, like many comic book characters, Skylar Storm is not imaginary, but a real person. It turns out she is in the hospital because all of her powers have been taken away by the "comic book" villain, The Annihilator. She regained her powers, but has ended up as the Annihilator's evil servant.

Speed Demon (real name James Sanders) is a recurring character in Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man, where he is a minor criminal with enhanced boots. Speed Demon was created by Roy Thomas and Sal Buscema.

The Spider-Slayers are highly-enhanced synthezoids created by Doctor Octopus. Each member was synthesized from the DNA of Spider-Man, whom the Spider-Slayers were also designed to eliminate. Spider Slayers were created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.
Death armor was a rare necromancy spell that surrounded the wizard in an aura that injured creatures upon contact. It could only be cast by necromancers.

Spidey (real name Peter Parker) is one of the main protagonists of the Disney Jr. animated series Spidey and his Amazing Friends. This variant of Spider-Man is depicted as a kid who fights crime alongside his friends: Ghost-Spider and Spin. He also teams up with other heroes to defeat evil foes and learn that teamwork is the best way to save the day. Spider-Man was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.

The Spirits of the Enchanted Forest, also known as the Elements, are five elemental beings prominent in Disney's 2019 animated feature film Frozen 2. Existing as mythical creatures that harness the magic of nature, these elements include water, fire, wind, earth, and a fifth spirit that bridges magic and humanity.

Steven Grant "Steve" Rogers (formerly known as Captain America) is a superhero from Marvel Comics. He made his debut in the Marvel Cinematic Universe in the 2011 film Captain America: The First Avenger, and is the eponymous protagonist of the Captain America films, and a featured character in the Avengers films. Captain America is a super-soldier from World War II who was frozen in ice for 70 years and then resumed his heroic duties. An idealistic American hero, Captain America advocates for freedom and justice as the leader and one of the founding members of the superhero team known as the Avengers. After the events of Captain America: Civil War, Steve became a fugitive from the authorities, known as Nomad. However, five years after the Infinity War, Captain America rejoins the Avengers to undo the Thanos' snap by traveling back in time to collect the Infinity Stones. They were successful in undoing the snap and managed to defeat an alternate version of Thanos and his armies. In the end of Avengers: Endgame, Captain America travelled back in time to return all of the Infinity Stones to their proper places, but instead of returning to the present, Steve stayed in an alternative timeline in the past so he could live out the rest of his life with the woman he loves, Peggy Carter. He then returned to the present in the original timeline as an elderly man and named Sam Wilson his successor by giving him his shield. Captain America was created by Jack Kirby and Joe Simon.

Dathlyr "the Hammer" Greybold was a dwarf fighter and adventurer based in Elturel in the Western Heartlands in the mid–14 century DR. Circa 1358 DR, he was one of the more important personalities of the city.
Sugracha the Eternal (also known by her alias Mrs. Sugarby) is a servant of Zhan Tiri and former pupil of Lord Demanitus who gathering her candidates to gain people's trust from Tangled: The Series.
Super Gilly is Gilbert Goof's superhero alter ego. He gets his powers by eating Super Goobers (peanuts), just like his uncle Goofy does to become Super Goof.
Supersonic Stu is a supervillain that appears in Big Hero 6: The Series. He is the grandson, and crime partner to, Supersonic Sue.
A dart of the hornets' nest, or a dart of the hornet's nest, was an extremely powerful thrown weapon.
Taranee Cook is one of the five main characters from the TV and comic book series W.I.T.C.H.

Tamatoa is the secondary antagonist of Disney's 2016 animated feature film Moana. He is a villainous giant crab who covets all things shiny and valuable. In an effort to exude beauty and superiority, Tamatoa displays his collected treasures atop his golden shell.
Thalia Grace is a supporting character in the Disney+ series Percy Jackson and the Olympians. She is the daughter of Zeus.
Deathbane was a sacred enchanted staff of powerful healing magic that belonged to a blind moon elf cleric of Mystra named Beriand circa 1369 DR.
The Bendu is an enormous being that is the physical embodiment of the center of the Force. As such, he is neither a practitioner of the light or dark sides of the Force, but sits in-between.

The Chairman is the main antagonist of the Disney Channel animated series The Ghost and Molly McGee. He was the tyrannical ruler of the Ghost World and the mysterious head of the Ghost Council until his rule was brought to an end by Molly McGee.

The Destructress (real name Lauren) is a former antagonist in the Disney Channel animated series Hamster & Gretel. She and her brother Lyle were given superpowers by the same aliens who gave Hamster and Gretel their powers, but they were told to use their powers for evil. However, in the show's second season, Lauren would come to prefer using her powers for good and switch over to the heroes' side.
Deathspike, also called the spear of skewering, was a powerful enchanted spear that could easily be used as a javelin.
The Jub Jub Bird is a major antagonist in Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland.
The Missile is one of the major villains from The Brave Little Toaster Goes to Mars.

"The Meanager" is Mr. Moseby's name as a supervillain. His minions are Esteban and Arwin. His only appearance is as the main antagonist in "Super Twins". The Meanager is, much to Moseby's shock, already a name that has been thought up by employees before Mr. Moseby himself. First, Zack and Cody wish upon a shooting star to be super heroes. They do this because they hate to be pushed around by Moseby and other adults. When they received powers, they had no idea that Mr. Moseby also wished upon the star to gain powers. The only difference is that Moseby used his powers for evil purposes instead of good ones. Mr. Moseby becomes "The Meanager" and sought on a personal goal to turn all kids into adults. The only thing stopping him is "Quick Guy" and "Brain Man". The heroes cause The Meanager's "Adultifier" ray to backfire on him, reverting him to an infant. Later, it was revealed that this was only a fantasy element, as Zack dreamed the entire event.
Dawnpike was an ancient elven enchanted spear created to be effective against the undead and drow.

Totoro (トトロ) is the titular deuteragonist from 1988 Hayao Miyazaki's Studio Ghibli film My Neighbor Totoro. He is a spirit of the forest who befriends Mei and Satsuki Kusakabe. A plush version of Totoro is owned by Bonnie in the 2010 Disney•Pixar animated feature film Toy Story 3.

Tridart, the Despair is one of the Four Knights of Hate, created by Nerissa. Tridart was made from the numerous icy stalactites found in the cave which Nerissa was sealed in. His form is that of a bald, muscular man with large, angel-like wings, and his weapon of choice is a short, double-edged axe. He represents the despair Nerissa felt in her prison. He was absorbed by Nerissa in the final battle, alongside Ember. He is voiced by Jim Cummings.

Trantor is the main antagonist of Ernest Scared Stupid. He was an ancient evil troll who desperately wanted to kill Ernest who is the descendant of the known "troll fighter", Phineas Worrell, who stopped his plans of resurrecting the evil troll race and overthrow humanity.
Dassar Truebow was one of Neverwinter's Rangers that operated throughout the Sword Coast North in the late 15 century DR.

Ultron is a supervillain from Marvel Comics who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He is a sentient, malevolent android created by Tony Stark meant for noble purposes, but after witnessing humanity's acts of violence, resolved to eradicate them from existence, leading him to become one of the Avengers' greatest enemies. Ultron was created by Roy Thomas and John Buscema.

Johnathan "John" F. Walker (formerly known as Captain America and currently known as U.S. Agent) is a Marvel Comics character who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He makes his debut in The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, which also marks the character's first adaptation in films and television. He is portrayed by Wyatt Russell. The Blip saw the return of half of all life return after five years, sending the world into turmoil. The United States government chose John Walker to become the new Captain America, believing him to be the embodiment of America's greatest values and an inspiration for everyone. Having taken on the new mantle, John selected Lemar Hoskins as his partner, and the two began working on apprehending the Flag Smashers and their leader, Karli Morgenthau. During this time, John took the super soldier serum, which granted him enhanced abilities. After taking the serum, John took a dark turn following the death of his best friend's death, which meant he was stripped of the Captain America title, until he was greeted by Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, who gave him another chance in the form of becoming known as the U.S. Agent. Three years after the promotion, John's wife Olivia left him and took their son as he continued to work for Valentina, who gave him orders to kill Yelena Belova, who in return was tasked to kill Ghost. After learning Val's true intentions, John joined Bucky Barnes, Yelena, Ghost, Red Guardian and Sentry to form the Thunderbolts, who

Uno (Italian for "one") is a character from the PKNA comic series. Uno is the AI of Ducklair Tower, created by inventor Everett Ducklair to have somebody of his same intellectual level to talk to. Even though generally Uno limits his function to the 151st secret floor, he actually is the whole tower, and can control any part of it. When Ducklair Tower is bought by Scrooge McDuck, he hires his nephew Donald to be its custodian and caretaker until there's enough tenants bringing their own staffs. Donald finds the 151st floor and investigates as The Duck Avenger, so he meets Uno, who becomes his ally and gives him access to Everett Ducklair's inventions. Very few people besides the Duck Avenger knows about Uno's existence.

A Daughter of Lolth, also referred to as Lolth's daughter, was a type of massive spider that could be found throughout the Sword Coast North region of Faerûn. They appeared in underground locations deep beneath the earth, and were used by drow during their raids on the surface world.

Ursula, Goddess of the Sea is a character featured in the ABC fantasy-drama series, Once Upon a Time, voiced by Yvette Nicole Brown. She makes her only appearance in the season three episode "Ariel". She is a legendary Sea Goddess, celebrated throughout the land. Having been unseen for thousands of years, she is thought to be a myth. She grants mermaids the ability to walk on land, once a year for twelve hours. She later makes her presence known to threaten the Evil Queen, after Regina impersonates her.

Vor is the final main antagonist of the Disney Jr. animated series Sofia the First, appearing in the series finale "Forever Royal". She was an evil sorceress who was imprisoned inside a magical locket and was found by Prisma.

Vic Madden (born Jack Thomas) is one of the main protagonists of the Disney Channel Original Series The Villains of Valley View. He is a retired supervillain from Centropolis formerly known by his supervillain name, Kraniac. He and Eva moved their family to Valley View, Texas after going on the run, in order to raise the kids and live a normal life. He is portrayed James Patrick Stuart.
A deathglyph was perhaps the most powerful handglyph weapon used by the Geomancers of Kadar, capable of instantly killing an enemy.

Warp Darkmatter, also known as Agent Z, is a former and corrupt space ranger and is the secondary antagonist and occasional antihero of the Disney•Pixar animated series Buzz Lightyear of Star Command. He was once a respected space ranger of Star Command and partner of Buzz Lightyear, but he had betrayed and violated the espionage act and treason for Star Command and has been secretly working for Zurg all along without getting caught since his academy days as a double agent. He eventually began working for him full-time as "Agent Z" after faking his death. His right arm is mechanical (with various weapon attachments) and was grafted to his body after becoming Agent Z. Warp often takes on assignments for Zurg and is paid quite handsomely (he owns a moon and a summer home). Though Buzz has vowed to bring him in for treason, he retains some hope that there is still some good in him.

Warmonga is one of the two overarching antagonists (alongside Warhok) of the fourth season of the Disney Channel animated TV series Kim Possible. She is a giant green-skinned female alien from the planet Lorwardia. She is a warrior woman standing somewhere around eight to ten feet in height. Warmonga wears a purple leotard-like bathing suit outfit and has a big booming voice, both befitting her amazonian image. Her name is a play on the term "war monger".
Wally B. is a bumblebee and one of the titular characters from The Adventures of André & Wally B.
Dead magic shield was a divine alteration spell used by priests devoted to Shaundakul, enabling them to create a shield of force.

Wanda Maximoff is a Marvel Comics character who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. She is an alternate reality counterpart of the Scarlet Witch. Wanda is portrayed by Elizabeth Olsen, who plays her mainstream counterpart. She was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

William Theodore "Will" Stronghold is the protagonist of Sky High, as well as the narrator of the film's opening and ending. He is the son of a famous superhero couple, the Commander and Jetstream, but does not seem to have inherited any powers until mid-film.

Willie the Giant is the main antagonist of the Mickey and the Beanstalk segment of the 1947 Disney package film Fun and Fancy Free and a supporting character of the rest of the Mickey Mouse franchise. He is a 62⅓-foot (19-meter)-tall, red-haired, and large-nosed magical giant, who, in stealing the Golden Harp, brings ruin to Happy Valley. Despite portraying the antagonist role in his debut appearance, Willie the Giant would later be recast as a good guy (or anti-hero) in many of his subsequent appearances, such as Mickey's Christmas Carol and Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, amongst others.

Dazlyn Grayshard was a shield dwarf prospector in the late 15th century DR. Together with her business partner, Norbus Ironrune, she discovered the ruins of the temple of Abbathor in the Sword Mountains.
Woodrow Wilkins is the protagonist of the 1981 film, Condorman. A wacky writer of comic books who suddenly becomes an agent of the C.I.A. under the codename "Condorman".

Yoda is a wise and sage-like diminutively-sized green alien Jedi Master and one of the main characters who appeared in the Star Wars universe. He appears as a major character in the second and third films of the original trilogy, as well as one of the major protagonists in the prequel trilogy, and made a cameo in Star Wars: The Last Jedi. Nobody knows what his species is. Yoda's adopted homeworld is Dagobah.

XL is an antagonist in the Disney/Pixar animated series Buzz Lightyear of Star Command. He is a flawed prototype of XR that was deactivated for his destructive programming and capabilities that seeks revenge on Star Command after being re-activated by Zurg. He appears in five episodes and eventually reforms, though much of his body is destroyed and rebuilt into a copy machine for the Star Command HQ.

A davit was a special form of crane system used on ships to hold or carry a ship's boat, that being smaller utility boats, such as skiffs or launches. This allowed such boats to be safely lowered into the water and more easily recovered. They came in several sizes, suitable for different sizes of boats.
Xenomorph XX121 (shortened as Xenomorphs or Xenos), also known as Internecivus raptus or simply the Aliens, are the main antagonistic species in the Alien franchise.

Experiment 000 (pronounced as "Experiment Zero"), or simply Zero, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and his earliest experiment before he began working with Hämsterviel and numbering his genetic creations. He is designed to be an ultimate killing monster and has enhanced his body with cybernetics at some point after escaping imprisonment. He appears as a minor antagonist in the second season of the Stitch! anime.
Zappapedes are large centipede-like creatures that reside in Amphibia's most mountainous regions. They get their name from their ability to manipulate electrical voltage.
Death's brink armor was a type of enchanted armor that made the wearer harder to kill.
A Giant Shy Guy is a much larger version of the Shy Guy found in Yoshi's New Island.

Giant Bowser X is a giant form of Bowser X and stronger variant of Giant Bowser who appears as a boss in the Battle Ring in Mario & Luigi: Dream Team. As with the previous battle, Bowser uses the same attacks, though they are a bit faster, stronger and some have slightly different patterns.

Inspector Gadget, also known simply as Inspector or Gadget (real name Augustin Tamare according to French press materials for his home series), is a bumbling detective cyborg who has starred in many animated TV series, specials, and two live-action films. He is well-known for the fact that his mechanical body contains a huge variety of gadgets, most of which are activated by him saying "Go-Go-Gadget-(name of gadget)". Inspector Gadget appeared as a guest star on The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! on two occasions. DIC Entertainment produced the 1983 animated series, and has used the character as the company mascot. As such, an animated version of Inspector Gadget is featured in the menu of the Mario's Greatest Movie Moments DVD, where he explains how to use the menu's various options.
Death of a Sailorman was a history book in three volumes that recorded the fall of Bloodsailer Trener B. Darven, scourge of the Sword Coast, penned some time before the late 14 century DR.

Jean-Pierre Colored Pencils the 12th, The Missile Maestro (also referred to simply as Colored Pencis or Color Pencil), is a member of the Legion of Stationery who guards a spool for the red streamer holding Princess Peach's Castle and serves as the boss of Overlook Tower in Paper Mario: The Origami King.

Mushroom Marauder and Jake the Crusher Fungus are a pair of two muscular Toad wrestlers who make a one-time appearance in the The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Tag Team Trouble." They are Toad's cousins, and he has at least one more cousin from another episode, "Mind Your Mummy Mommy, Mario." A flyer from the Mushroom Wrestling Federation features both Mushroom Marauder and Jake the Crusher Fungus on it.

The Nimbus are a humanoid species with cloud-like bodies in Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars. Their homeland is Nimbus Land, a monarchy ruled over by King Nimbus and Queen Nimbus. The most notable member of the species is their son, Mallow, who serves as one of Mario's party members.
Dazar was a human fighter from the Hordelands, in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Wingo is a massive crow bird and the main villan antagonist of Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker.

Dark Lord Hum Gree, also known as simply Hum Gree, is a giant blue demon in a black robe who appears in Ashley & Red's stage in WarioWare Gold. His name is a pun on "hungry". He is famous in the demon realms for eating obsessively, an action he is unable to stop doing no matter how much he eats. As such, his mouth is always open, and even his uvula has a face that can eat food. This fame does not appear to extend to the rest of the world, as Ashley is unaware of Hum Gree.

E.C. The Extra Creepy is a robotic, alien entity made to resemble a female human and a character from The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!. Her name is a reference E.T., the alien creature from the classic film . According to E.C.'s quality sheet print-out from the computer dating service, she is an "out of this world girl, with head in the clouds, loves to travel..." and "comes with a two year warranty". In The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live-action segment "E.C. The Extra Creepy", E.C., through a computer dating service, is set-up on a date with Mario. Going to Mario Brothers Plumbing, her appearance preceded by flickering lights, an earthquake and smoke, E.C. introduces herself to Mario. After introducing himself to E.C., Mario asks for her hand, which E.C. literally gives him - removing her hand and giving it to a shocked Mario. After this incident, Luigi begins trying to tell a lovestruck Mario how odd E.C. is, as E.C. wanders around Mario Brothers Plumbing. Rebuffing Luigi's claims about E.C.'s strangeness, Mario decides to go on his date with E.C., who has just revealed some of her abilities, such as being able to take a bite out of a wrench and light a lightbulb just by touching it. Mario and E.C. later return from their date, which was seemingly in E.C.'s spaceship, with Mario carrying E.C. back into Mario Brothers Plumbing. Setting E.C. down on the floor, Mario and Luigi eventually come to the realization that E.C. is a robot when she begins to malfunction slightly,
Defending was a weapon quality that let a magical weapon aid its wielder in defense.

The Fire God (also referred to as the Big Kahuna) is a large, burly inhabitant of the island of Waki-Waki in Lava Land. As his name suggests, the Fire God is a deity, though what powers he may have are not shown. In The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Too Hot to Handle", Mario, Luigi, Toad and Princess Toadstool travel to Waki-Waki in search of the Fire God, who has promised to help them free the Mushroom Kingdom from King Koopa. As is eventually revealed, the Fire God has been captured by King Koopa and Fryguy, who are keeping him imprisoned in a giant, snow- and ice-filled bottle. With the Fire God, who he eventually plans to throw into his Lava Machine, as his prisoner, King Koopa tricks the inhabitants of Waki-Waki into believing that he is the Fire God as a part of his plan to capture Princess Toadstool. After King Koopa and Fryguy are defeated by Mario (and the Lava Machine destroyed), the Fire God, free from the giant, frozen bottle, sends a smoke signal to him, as well as the inhabitants of Waki-Waki. Interpreting the Fire God's smoke signal, Scooter, the leader of Waki-Waki, reveals that the Fire God wants to throw a spaghetti luau for Mario. At this spaghetti luau, the Fire God acts as the spaghetti chef, using the chained and caged Fryguy to cook the spaghetti.

Game and Watch are two humans that appear in [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D33E41t5xOs a British commercial] for Game & Watch. They wear hats and are depicted only in silhouette. ]] Game and Watch are seen kidnapping the various elements seen in Donkey Kong at night to trap them in said game or Mario Bros., first by pushing one of "the world's most dangerous buildings" through unseen means, then making Donkey Kong (described as one of "the fiercest gorillas on Earth") break from his zoo cage by luring him with a banana, then finally using clubs to assault Mario, described as one of the "toughest Italians", in a park. It is suggested in the dialogue that Game and Watch have kidnapped other Italians, buildings, and gorillas.
Bowser is the main antagonist of the Super Mario franchise. His history spans decades of media primarily in video games, but it also includes cartoons, books, and other promotional materials.

Delg Ironstar, also called Delg Hammerhand, was a dwarf warrior and adventurer and part of the Company of the Bright Spear in the mid–14 century DR. He was also a member of the Harpers and one of the last members of the legendary noble clan of dwarves, Clan Ironstar.

The Kōmori Sentai Komorinjā are a group of four costumed Komorin (one red, one blue, one green, and one black) that appear as the antagonists of the first chapter of Super Mario-kun Volume 10, during the Mario & Wario arc. They are based off the , the first installment of the Japanese superhero TV series . They are hired by Wario to stop Mario, Yoshi, and Bowser-Wanda to leave Kōri no Dōkutsu. Initially armed with their fists and an Unibo shooter, whose projectiles are sent back at them, taking advantage of Mario and Yoshi getting stuck on some Nebaneba Blocks, they summon their robot formation, the Komoringā. To fight their robot, Bowser-Wanda summons the Mario Zone robot and, after dealing with a giant pipe bucket stuck on his robot's head, Mario comes out victorious, overwhelming the Komoringā with all the content the robot vomited out from dizziness.

Manteau Cutter is a move performed by Cape Mario Great in the Super Mario Bros. 4: Super Mario World 7 of Super Mario Kodansha manga. After bliding the Chitei Kaijū Indy, Mario uses its sunglasses x-ray vision to locate the princesses trapped inside and locate a weak spot. After that, Mario throws his cape like a shuriken, splitting the monster in half and destroying it. The princesses, stored in his belly, start falling, but Bowser swoops in and takes them to his base.

Mega Baby Bowser, also known as Big Baby Bowser, is an enormous form Baby Bowser takes in many Yoshi games. He often serves as the final boss of a game. Unlike Giant Bowser, Mega Baby Bowser's size has stayed roughly the same across the franchise. The method used to enlarge Baby Bowser varies, but regardless of method Baby Bowser becomes Mega Baby Bowser after defeating him normally.
Dendritic crystal armor was heavy armor made by dwarves from dendritic seed crystals grown deep underground.

Megaton Koopa Hō is a form that Bowser takes in Super Mario-kun volume 14. He takes the shape of a bazooka, vaguely similar to a Super Scope. Mario, Luigi, and Yoshi end up in the future, where Bowser won over the Mario Brothers and is ruling the Mushroom Kingdom. When future Bowser finally meet up with his old rivals, he shows off his new magic powers by transforming into the Megaton Koopa Hō to shoot them, but without someone to hold him or press the trigger, he remains immobile. Taking advantage of this, the Toads of the future, freed by Mario from the Koopalings, kick and punch him, putting an end to his domain. Defeated, Bowser takes inspiration for a photo of Baby Mario and uses his magic powers to go back in time and prevent Mario's birth, starting off the Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island arc.

E-123 Omega, commonly known as simply Omega, is a crossover character from the franchise who has made some appearances in the Super Mario franchise within the Mario & Sonic series. Omega is a robot who was created by Dr. Eggman to contain Shadow. Omega first physically appears in where he, Shadow, and Rouge team up to form , though he was mentioned in released a few weeks prior. Shadow and Rouge go on to be Omega's closest allies. His voice is provided by in Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Winter Games and in Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games and Mario & Sonic at the Sochi 2014 Olympic Winter Games.

The pipe creatures are two giant characters on The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3, where they appear in the episode "A Toadally Magical Adventure". Originally, they were normal pipes, but Toad transforms them into live beings with the Wizard King of the West's wand. At first, they are peaceful, as Toad simply instructs them to make noises out of their pipe holes, but he keeps bossing them around to make louder and faster noises. This causes the pipe creatures to become angry, so they steal the wand from Toad and bring to life a stack of blocks to terrorize him. King Koopa later comes and sees that the pipe creatures have the wand. Koopa then instructs some Boomerang Brothers to get the wand. The pipe creatures dodge the boomerangs with ease and laugh, but they are caught off guard when the boomerangs come back, and they lose the wand. Koopa then freezes them with the wand. Later, Bully Koopa makes the pipe creatures play a game of catch with the Mario Bros. and Toad as the balls. Cheatsy Koopa makes a giant Nipper Plant attack Mario, but the blue pipe creature is hit instead. Mario then wrenches the purple pipe creature's arm off to free Toad. However, the blue one catches Mario again, and it is then destroyed after he turns into Raccoon Mario. Later on, the Wizard King arrives. He transforms the pipe creatures into big hands, which pick up Koopa and the Koopalings, then drop them in a pipe back to Koopa Kastle.

Derdek Deepingdell was a male dwarf fighter and the proprietor of the Bear's Den inn of Thunderstone in the late 1360s DR. Derdek was quite short and wide for a dwarf and bore a very bushy beard. All in all, he resembled a small bear himself.

Qix Daiō is Bowser's third alter-ego in the Super Mario Land manga miniseries of the KC Deluxe series, during the events of the first two chapters of the fourth issue. Bowser wears a black Samurai-like helmet with two big triangular crests behind each of the winglets. A giant Game Boy is used like a chest piece. He also wears a black cape (red in one illustration) and pauldrons. Like always, nobody, neither minions nor enemies, refers to Qix Daiō as "Bowser". While Princess Daisy visits the Mushroom Kingdom to see Mario, Qix Daiō kidnaps her by locking her behind the screen of his Game Boy armor and challenges Mario to save by retrieving the pieces of the key to free her by beating his minions around the world at Qix. Mario, followed by Luigi and Peach, accepts the challenge. In , the trio beats a Suu, and Qix Daiō punishes its failure by pulverizing him. In Africa, after Gao loses, Qix Daiō attaches a rope-line to it and a Fuse follows it and explodes it. In China, Qix Daiō buffs Pionpi to make things easier for it, but loses and it is reduced to dust. The key is restored, but before freeing Daisy, Qix Daiō teleports the heroes to the rooftop pool of the Qix Biru in New York City, where they will face him in a 2 player battle. Qix Daiō is aided by Hiyoihoi, who uses his Ganchan to keep away the floating Qix from their Marker. After the Qix breaks Mario's Marker in half, almost making him fall off the building, Qix Daiō attempts to push him off. Daisy, still trapped inside th

Quasi Obliterator is the final boss of and the last boss that Mario faces in the game adaptation in the Super Mario Land 4 manga. It is a giant sentient fly head that shoots lightnings. While in the game, Quasi Obliterator is the leader of Reticulon, he is demoted due to Torino Daiō taking that role in the manga. Quasi Obliterator is hidden behind Xenocrypt's wall, in the core of Reticulon (or, as the game ending suggests, he is the core itself). Mario has no trouble whatsoever in taking him down, but once defeated, Torino Daiō operates a holographic machine that tricks Mario into thinking into having to redo the mission from scratch.

The Vellumentals are a group of elemental, deity-like creatures that reside in their own Vellumental shrines and temples, acting as bosses in Paper Mario: The Origami King. Certain in-game text suggests that they were not always made of origami. When each Vellumental is defeated, it unveils a Bibliofold that contains instructions on how to fold into them. This allows Olivia to transform into one via a corresponding Magic Circle, allowing Mario to access its elemental powers. Each Vellumental will also become available for a timed refight using a Bossotronic Fighter in Toad Town's Battle Lab. During certain Wave Battles, an enemy may hold a random Vellumental Magic Circle, which if defeated will allow Olivia to transform into that Vellumental and attack all enemies with 50 damage in the next turn, or the next wave if all enemies in the current wave are defeated. However, the Magic Circle disappears from the enemy if Mario fails to solve the ring puzzle. King Olly also possesses the ability to turn into each of the Vellumentals in the first stage of his boss fight. In their original origami forms, the Vellumentals have no eyes. When Olivia transforms into a Vellumental, it gains eyes and a two-pointed crown on its head. When King Olly becomes a Vellumental, alongside eyes, a three-pointed crown, and a large flap of hair like Olly's, the majority of their skin turns purple. The Vellumentals appear to have a connection with Shangri-Spa, as the Sea Tower, the gateway to Shangri-Sp
The Delras was the spelljamming ship of the lich Demchungchumrub.

Jack is rumored to be the most powerful human biotic ever encountered. Very little additional data regarding Jack is available, except that the subject has a history of violence and should be approached carefully. Currently, Jack is being held on the turian prison ship Purgatory. Cerberus has negotiated for the prisoner's release.
Ravagers are synthetic-organic creatures derived from rachni through the use of Reaper technology. They appear in 2186, where they act as mobile artillery pieces for Reaper ground forces.
Derval's Bright Blade was a weapon-smithy in Daggerford on the Sword Coast in the late 1360s DR, owned by the dwarf master smith Derval Ironeater.
Demonger J5 is a bat-like Mechanical Beast from Mazinger Z vs. Devilman and later it is seen in Mazinkaiser (OVA).
Dogla S1 is a Mechanical Beast that is connected to Magla F2 to attack the Kabuto family's new home to capture Koji Kabuto.
Bossman B9 is a Mechanical Beast designed to resemble Boss Borot in the TV Magazine manga, it was sent by Count Brocken to destroy the Mazinger Z.
Delver's Plate was a suit of plate mail armor, worn by the great Waterdhavian general, Delver Kinlake.
Damdam L2 is a Mechanical Beast sent to wreak havoc on a nearby city and the Photon Power Laboratory with Koji Kabuto's assassination taking place.
Bombcat T3 is a Mechanical Beast used by Dr. Hell in one of his plans to take over Mazinger Z.
Genocider F9 is a large jet plane-like Mechanical Beast that appeared as the monster of the week in episode 34 of the Mazinger Z anime.
The Delryn family shield was an enchanted medium shield that was an heirloom passed down within the noble Delryn family of Amn.
Drago Ω1 is a Ghost Mechanical Beast in Mazinkaiser that was the first to be revealed.
Garalia (Sentoujuu Garariya) is a Superhuman Warrior Beast with a psychotic attitude, fitting the image and mindset of a berserker.
An unnamed Mechanical Beast modeled after and piloted by Dr. Hell that served as the final boss of the Mazinger Z video game.
Delvon Ludwig was a priest of Torm who lived in the Sword Coast North during the late 15 century DR.
Groizer X12 is a bombing Mechanical Beast that was among the Groizer X robots used by Count Brocken to attack the Saluud.
Garuda C3 is a Mechanical Beast used by Dr. Hell, along with Balga M4, to be destroyed and implant a Kedora on Mazinger Z.
Gratonios is one of the first Warrior Beasts (a superhuman at that) that appeared in the series. It appeared in the final episode of Mazinger Z along with Pilanias.

Deeping Cave was a cavern in Kryptgarden Forest on the Sword Coast North. It was the lair of the green dragon Claugiyliamatar, a.k.a. Old Gnawbone, but its name came from local humans, who named it for some forgotten reason before Old Gnawbone arrived.
Euingaros was a Superhuman type Warrior Beast who was partnered alongside Dagora in episode 21 of Great Mazinger.
Goram is a Superhuman Warrior Beast of the Mycenae Empire that appeared in the Great Mazinger manga.

as seen in the Toei version of UFO Robot Grendizer]] Born as the crown prince of Planet Fried, Duke Fried lived a peaceful life until the ruthless Vegan Empire invaded his home. In a desperate attempt to save his people, Duke stole the powerful super robot, Grendizer, and fled to Earth, crash-landing in Japan. Taken in by Dr. Umon, he adopted the alias "Daisuke Umon" and lived in hiding, concealing his alien heritage while working on a farm. When the Vega Empire set its sights on Earth, Duke Fried emerged as humanity’s defender, piloting Grendizer against the alien invaders. As time goes on, Duke forms close bonds with humans, including Koji Kabuto, the pilot of Mazinger Z. Together, they fought the relentless forces of the Vega Empire, protecting Earth from destruction. As the rightful heir to Fried, Duke struggled with the responsibility of protecting Earth while longing to return to his home planet. Despite his inner conflict, he remained steadfast, and Grendizer the defender of Earth against the threat posed by the Vega Empire.
